correctness.rationale: The factorization \(F(n)=\prod_{p\mid n}p^{(a+sb)\nu_p(n)-sb}(p^s-1)^b\) is exact. Properly nested prime supports are impossible without the hypothesis \(a\ge sb\). For incomparable supports, cancellation of common cyclotomic factors gives \(L_S\mid C_T\) and \(L_T\mid C_S\). Using \(p^s-1<p^s\) and multiplying the two inequalities yields the claimed strict product obstruction. When \(a<sb\), exponent-one unique primes contribute negative exponent \(a-sb\), while every repeated unique prime contributes at least \(2a>0\); hence a collision must have an exponent-one unique prime. If both integers are powerful this is impossible, while equal support forces equal exponents by unique factorization. The packaged verifier checks the powerful corollary on a broad finite parameter grid from the actual package path.

value.rationale: The focal paper explicitly isolates \(s\ge3,\ a<sb\) as its unresolved injectivity regime. The new inequality preserves quantitative information exactly where the published cyclic size contradiction stops working. It identifies the squarefree layer as necessary for any counterexample and closes the entire standard infinite class of powerful integers, rather than an arbitrary bounded slice. This is a motivated structural obstruction that can materially narrow both theoretical and computational searches for a counterexample.
